title: Injectivity of the canonical local completion comparison
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak m$ its maximal ideal, $C=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $Q=\{\mathfrak q\subset S: \mathfrak q\text{ prime},\ \mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p\}$, and $D_{\mathfrak q}=\varprojlim_n S_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak q S_{\mathfrak q})^n$. Let $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:A\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ be the canonical localized map. Let $f:C\otimes_R S\to\prod_{\mathfrak q\in Q}D_{\mathfrak q}$ be an $S$-algebra map (tensor product as in [def-weil-module-base-change]). Assume that for every $\mathfrak q\in Q$, $n\geq0$, $a\in C$ and $r\in A$, the equality $a_n=r\bmod\mathfrak m^n$ implies $f(a\otimes1)_{\mathfrak q,n}=\varphi_{\mathfrak q}(r)\bmod(\mathfrak q S_{\mathfrak q})^n$. Then $f$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 07N9, lemma-completion-finite-extension, proof: quotient products, finite-after-completion (0394), and completion-tensor (00MA)

proof.text: Put A = R_p and B = A tensor_R S. B is finite over the Noetherian local ring A. Localization identifies the primes of B over its maximal ideal m with Q, and their local rings with S_q. Every B/m^n B for n > 0 is Artinian. Its canonical map to the product of S_q/m^n S_q is an isomorphism by Tags 00JA and 00CT.

These canonical maps commute with reduction. Thus the map from the m-adic completion of B into the product of the m-adic completions of S_q is injective: if every component is zero, each quotient coordinate is zero by the quotient product isomorphism, and the original compatible sequence is zero.

In S_q, the extended ideal m S_q has radical q S_q. Noetherianity gives a power of q S_q contained in m S_q; the converse inclusion is immediate. Tag 0394 identifies the two completions by the identity on S_q. Therefore replacing the factors by the maximal-ideal completions preserves injectivity.

Tag 00MA identifies C tensor_A B with the m-adic completion of B, and tensor cancellation identifies C tensor_A B with C tensor_R S. Under this canonical comparison the resulting map sends a tensor s to the tuple g_q(a) times s. The hypothesis on f determines g_q: choose a representative of each quotient coordinate of a and apply the displayed equation, then use extensionality of compatible sequences. S-linearity and tensor induction identify f with this comparison map. Composing the injections proves the claim. The zero algebra and empty Q are included: B/m^n B and its completion are then zero.

theorem completion_tensor_localMaps_injective
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    let A := Localization.AtPrime p
    let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
    let C := AdicCompletion m A
    let Q := p.primesOver S
    let D := fun q : Q ↦
      AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1))
        (Localization.AtPrime q.1)
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := C) (B := S)
    ∀ (f : (C ⊗[R] S) →ₐ[S] (∀ q : Q, D q)),
      (∀ (q : Q) (n : ℕ) (a : C) (r : A),
        evalₐ m n a = Ideal.Quotient.mk (m ^ n) r →
        evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1)) n
            (f (a ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S)) q) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1)) ^ n)
            (Localization.localRingHom p q.1 (algebraMap R S)
              (Ideal.LiesOver.over (P := q.1) (p := p)) r)) →
      Function.Injective f
